authoredNote: Lines read off `nl -ba` of this file: cb() 16, publishedNested() 17, assign(1) 18. The spelled target contains U+0000; JSON spells it `\u0000`.
rationale: PINS THE LOCAL-BINDING CLAIM (D7) IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Positive: a call to a PARAMETER (`cb()`) is re-spelled `outer\u0000cb` with `meta.localBinding: true` — the family publishes no parameter as a symbol, so the spelled target can never be refuted by the declaration key space, and the arbiter verifies it from its own spelling. A call to a locally-declared lambda (`assign(1)`) is the same class (`outer\u0000assign`), and its argument text keeps the row's line. NEGATIVE: a nested FUNCTION DECLARATION can be published as a symbol by this analyzer, so its call stays the bare name (`publishedNested`) — re-spelling it would withdraw a binding that may legitimately resolve; the fixture's forbid row makes that over-claim red. This is the difference between the local-binding class and the imported-binding class: the former is verified by spelling, the latter by the file's import evidence.

forbidRelationships.note: a PUBLISHED nested declaration must not be re-spelled — its edge may resolve
the bare spelling must not survive: one row, re-spelled in place (never two rows for one edge)
